about: Recipes: for a failure class that keeps coming back (the finding log, lib/findingRepeats.js), what would guard it in this stack. One recipe per class and stack; the first whose `when` holds is shown on the card ledger-recipes. `when` uses the conditions of the cards (lib/checksCatalog.js, plugin/docs/checks.md), `cards` names cards that already do the work, and `examples` are facts the recipe must hold for (hit) and must not hold for (miss); a test checks them. A project adds, replaces (same id) or removes (`off: true`) a recipe in docs/queue/checks/recipes.json. A database recipe (`db: true`, access control and migration) needs db-probes-on (learning.dbProbes, off by default) and a local database (has-local-database or local-db:<engine>) in its `when`, and its text names the host check and the rollback; Build as gate adds the shared database guard to the mission.

recipes.title: A lint rule for results nobody checks
recipes.text: Turn on @typescript-eslint/no-floating-promises (and no-misused-promises) in the project's eslint setup, or a no-restricted-syntax rule for the exact call that was left unchecked, and run lint in gates.quick.

recipes.title: A lint rule and a test on the error path
recipes.text: A no-restricted-syntax rule in the project's eslint setup for the call whose result was left unchecked (or eslint-plugin-promise catch-or-return), and a test that makes that call fail and expects the error to reach the caller.

recipes.title: Ruff rules for swallowed errors, or a test on the error path
recipes.text: Ruff rules for swallowed errors (BLE001 blind except, S110 try-except-pass, E722 bare except) in the project's ruff setup, or a pytest test that makes the failing call raise and expects the error to reach the caller.

recipes.title: A type check in the gates and CI
recipes.text: A type check in gates.quick and CI: tsc --noEmit for TypeScript, mypy or pyright for Python, with a mild setting and a baseline for the errors there are today.

recipes.title: The type check in CI too
recipes.text: The type check runs, but not in CI: add it to the CI workflow, so a change that skips the local gates is caught too.

recipes.title: A secret scan in CI
recipes.text: gitleaks (or trufflehog) in CI on every push, with an allow list where each entry says why it is safe.

recipes.title: A narrower allow list for the scan
recipes.text: The scan runs in CI but this one got past it: check the allow list (every entry needs a reason), and add the file kind or folder it missed to the scan's paths.

recipes.title: Time limits and a worker cap for the tests
recipes.text: A time limit per test above the default and a cap on the workers (vitest or jest --maxWorkers) in the gate command, so parallel tracks on one machine do not starve each other. A weakened test: restore it, and keep testWeakening.enabled on.

recipes.title: Time limits and a worker cap for pytest
recipes.text: pytest-timeout with a time limit per test, and a cap on pytest-xdist workers (-n 2 rather than -n auto) in the gate command. A weakened test: restore it, and keep testWeakening.enabled on.

recipes.title: pgTAP probes for the access rules, with supabase test db
recipes.text: pgTAP probes in supabase/tests, run with supabase test db against the local stack (supabase start): per test user set the role and JWT claims, then show that another user's rows stay hidden and a forbidden write is refused (throws_ok). Each file is BEGIN; ... ROLLBACK;, and the gate first checks that the host is localhost, 127.0.0.1 or ::1 and stops otherwise. Never --linked.

recipes.title: pgTAP probes for the access rules, with pg_prove
recipes.text: pgTAP probes run with pg_prove against the local or container database (docker compose, testcontainers): SET ROLE to each test user, then show that another user's rows stay hidden and a forbidden write is refused (throws_ok). Each file is BEGIN; ... ROLLBACK;, and the gate first checks that the host is localhost, 127.0.0.1, ::1 or the container it started, and stops otherwise.

recipes.title: Access rule tests against a throwaway database
recipes.text: A test in the project's own test runner against a throwaway database (testcontainers, or the compose service): one test per rule that must refuse (another user's rows, a forbidden write), each in a transaction rolled back at the end. Before it writes, the test checks that the host is localhost, 127.0.0.1, ::1 or the container it started, and stops otherwise.

recipes.title: Migrations from empty and schema probes, with supabase db reset
recipes.text: supabase db reset on the local stack builds the database from every migration, then supabase test db runs pgTAP schema probes (has_table, col_type_is, policies_are) for what the migration made; the same two in CI from empty. Probes are BEGIN; ... ROLLBACK;, and the gate first checks that the host is localhost, 127.0.0.1 or ::1 and stops otherwise. Never --linked.

recipes.title: Migrations from empty and schema probes, with pg_prove
recipes.text: Every migration from an empty local or container database with the project's migrate tool, then pgTAP schema probes with pg_prove (has_table, col_type_is) for what the migration made; the same in CI on a service container. Probes are BEGIN; ... ROLLBACK;, and the gate first checks that the host is localhost, 127.0.0.1, ::1 or the container it started, and stops otherwise.

recipes.title: Migrations from empty on a throwaway database
recipes.text: Every migration from an empty throwaway database (testcontainers, or the compose service), then a test in the project's own test runner that checks the schema the migration made; the same in CI. Tests that write roll back, and the run first checks that the host is localhost, 127.0.0.1, ::1 or the container it started, and stops otherwise.
